{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABbXZIbQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhE7zzc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 122, "title": "Investigate recurring post-merge main Chromium acceptance failures and stabilize real-Wasm browser tests", "body": "## Problem

The **Emulator acceptance** workflow passes on feature/PR branches yet has failed on **two consecutive merge-to-`main` runs**, while GitHub Pages deployment succeeds:

| Source | Commit | Emulator acceptance | GitHub Pages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR #117 merge | `f8c17052e3ddb9f60bb12ad442b626d7ff2d8a46` | [run #41146277227](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41146277227) **failure** | [success](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41146277232) |
| PR #121 merge | `d1f3c35eaf4ab96e1aa3fcdf3765d9327484081e` | [run #41158209467](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41158209467) **failure** | [success](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41158209470) |
| PR #117 branch | `24e5e38a8a6b` | [run #41143426391](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41143426391) **success** | N/A |
| PR #121 branch | `800b5a1f35cd` | [run #41155305993](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/41155305993) **success** | N/A |

Both failed `main` workflows show **`Run npm test` as the failed step** in the `native-and-browser` job; fixture preparations, formatting, Clippy, `cargo test --locked`, dependency installation and browser installation completed successfully. GitHub Actions uploaded **`browser-failure-traces`** artifacts in each run. The **specific failing test in the latest main run has not yet been independently identified**, so do not assume both failures have the same cause.

[PR #121](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/121) reports that the earlier main run (#41146277227) had **167 passing tests and one 120-second `fragmented16` HDD investigation timeout** at the project root. That test passed under the contributor's local Playwright environment, and the full local suite passed **194 real Chromium tests across both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`** using **four workers** (and temporary alternate server ports). This points to possible environment/CPU contention or test timeout behavior but does **not** prove a flaky-test-only root cause, nor does it account for the new main failure without inspecting its traces.

The latest `main` is `d1f3c35e` (PR #121); Issue #120 is completed and the public demo's Ap DOS/Auto media routing is merged. **The separate deployment success does not mean acceptance passed.** There are currently no open Issues/PRs to track this recurring CI failure.

## Expected outcome

Restore a reliably green **`Emulator acceptance` on `main`** with meaningful, full **native and actual production-Wasm Chromium coverage** for both serving roots, preserving correctness and avoiding cosmetic CI workarounds. Diagnose the concrete failure, distinguish an actual emulator/guest regression from test harness timing/worker resource contention, fix the underlying problem or appropriately bounded harness issue, and provide reproducible evidence.

Do **not** weaken acceptance assertions, mark tests flaky without evidence, broadly skip tests, omit the project-root variant, disable either URL root, fake guest output, increase timeouts arbitrarily, or downgrade real-Wasm execution to host-scripted expectations.

## Context and reproduction

- CI definition: [`.github/workflows/emulator.yml`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/.github/workflows/emulator.yml) — Ubuntu 24.04, 45-minute job, fixture preparation and license checks, Rust fmt/Clippy/tests, `npm ci`, Playwright Chromium install, **`npm test`**, and a seven-day failure trace artifact.
- Playwright configuration: [`playwright.config.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/playwright.config.js) — `fullyParallel: true`, per-test timeout 45s, assertion timeout 12s, two projects (`local` at `127.0.0.1:8000/`, `pages` at `127.0.0.1:8001/pc98-rust/`), each with its own local web server and trace retention on failure.
- A previous HDD-investigation timeout appeared even with working kernel/IDE tests; reference [`tests/browser/hdd-investigation.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tests/browser/hdd-investigation.spec.js). Confirm its actual CI budget/timeout semantics and whether the test is truly the latest failing case.
- Both failed main runs have GitHub Actions artifacts named **`browser-failure-traces`** (saved `test-results/`). Review them *within their retention period*, along with the complete `npm test` output. Don't infer a test's failure from only the workflow step result.

## Investigation plan

1. **Collect exact evidence for each failing run:** identify test names, project root, failure type, timeouts, retries (if any), screenshot/trace detail, elapsed time, workers, fixture loading status, CPU/IDE/IRQ counters and whether failures differ. Use GitHub job logs and trace artifacts when accessible; if access is unavailable, say so and regenerate equivalent evidence with a reproducible run.
2. **Compare environments and resources:** `main` push vs PR event, same code tree vs merge commit, Ubuntu runner cores/CPU contention, Playwright default worker count vs contributor's **`--workers=4`** baseline, simultaneous heavyweight HDD/VM86 tests across two roots, dev-server ports, browser startup and timeout accounting.
3. **Reproduce with legal fixtures:** run the full documented suite on an equivalent CI-like Linux environment and compare the default worker setting, a justified bounded worker cap, and any targeted diagnostic loop. Collect timings and target-specific guest progress. Keep a realistic full acceptance path for the actual production Rust/Wasm image.
4. **Implement the smallest evidenced correction:** e.g. CPU-resource-aware test concurrency, isolation for expensive tests, deterministic waits tied to guest state, or an actual emulator/harness bug fix. Base limits on measured runner capacity and execution budgets, not blind timeout inflation. Ensure existing failures still fail on genuinely incorrect guest/CPU/IDE behavior.
5. **Verify on fresh workflows:** explain the exact before/after failure mechanism and demonstrate passing affected tests and *full* acceptance on `main`-equivalent content with both URL roots. Check a genuine merge-to-main CI run after merge as a **separate nonblocking operational follow-up**, not as a pre-merge approval prerequisite.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Identify the **exact failing test(s) and mechanism** of both main runs #41146277227 and #41158209467 from logs/traces or re-created equivalent evidence. If only one run's logs are accessible, say so and explain uncertainty; do not claim the failures were identical without proof.
- [ ] Distinguish a real emulator correctness/guest progress regression from browser scheduling/resource/timing. Document runner and worker-count differences, where each failure occurs, and what independent observations support the diagnosis.
- [ ] Add an appropriately narrow change addressing the demonstrated root cause, or establish and document a reproducible environmental failure with an actionable separate follow-up if no in-repo fix is justified. Avoid skipped tests, hidden retries and unjustified timeout increases; preserve exact guest-owned success/failure assertions, disk invariants, and full suite coverage.
- [ ] Exercise the previously failing test(s) multiple times under measured CI-like conditions, then run **the complete real production-Wasm Chromium suite** at **both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`**, including the HDD controls and new Ap/Auto media-routing tests, with cold/reset checks unchanged.
- [ ] Run/report applicable full fixture preparation and license checks, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Rust/Wasm build and exact approved-assets audit. Record actual failures, reruns, worker options and all test counts; do not cite old PR results as new verification.
- [ ] Explain the issue and correction in concise English developer/validation notes. If `main` remains red for an independent issue, open a linked English `task` Issue and explicitly report the pending item; never claim the CI is fully fixed without evidence.
- [ ] Review with Issue → PR → review → merge workflow. A **merge-triggered main CI** or published Pages check is **not** a pre-merge blocker. No manual game playtest, proprietary HDI, adult content or physical hardware required. Do not copy/translate other emulator code.

## Optional validation

Repeat the default Ubuntu CI run multiple times with an otherwise identical code tree and record test runtime distributions, rare worker starvation patterns, any flaky test and resource data. If useful, compare single-root focused runs to the complete two-root parallel suite; focused green tests alone are not a substitute for the complete suite.

## Required post-merge verification

None for pre-merge acceptance. If fresh `main` deployment workflows continue to fail, report the exact workflow URL and create or update a separate `task` Issue for that post-merge operational failure; never misrepresent a PR-branch green check as a successful main push.
